subject.title: Discord plugin does not auto-reconnect after 1006 WS close (forces full gateway restart, kills in-flight turns)

question: Should maintainers require a current-main public-transition root cause before accepting a Discord abnormal-close recovery patch, or sponsor a bounded close-handler mitigation based on the repeated live production logs?
rationale: The bug has strong live release evidence and high user impact, but the previous direct mitigation was closed after maintainer review found the stale reconnect-disabled state was not reachable through known public transitions.

options.title: Require Current-Main Root-Cause Proof
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for live or harness proof that identifies the transition suppressing reconnect before a new code PR lands.

options.title: Sponsor A Bounded Mitigation
options.body: Allow an owner-reviewed close-handler mitigation with promoted operational diagnostics while separately tracking the hidden transition if it recurs.

options.title: Add Only Operator Fallback
options.body: Defer automatic recovery and expose a channel-scoped reconnect action, accepting that the primary websocket recovery bug remains unresolved.

recommendation.title: Require Current-Main Root-Cause Proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for live or harness proof that identifies the transition suppressing reconnect before a new code PR lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest recent history across Discord gateway lifecycle, supervisor, and the merged retry-boundary fix adjacent to this issue.
